defs.def: done, chosen, etc. without sb deciding in advance what is going to happen, or without any regular pattern 随机的，随意的（非事先决定或不规则）

ex.s: Participants were randomly divided into two groups: the “beauty” group was asked to actively consider and then rate the beauty of each object they viewed, while the control group just matched a line drawing of the object with the artwork itself.
ex.t: 参与者被随机分为两组：“美”组被要求主动思考并为所看到的每件物品的美打分，而对照组只是将物品的线描图与艺术品本身进行匹配。

ex.s: We cannot even entirely control who we will meet in our lives: a difference of minutes or even seconds determines random meetings that can change our fate.
ex.t: 我们甚至无法完全控制我们一生中会遇到谁：几分钟甚至几秒钟的差异就决定了可能改变我们命运的偶然相遇。

ex.s: I had a strong urge to look at the random things that were being flashed before my eyes!
ex.t: 我有一种强烈的冲动，想看看那些在我眼前闪过的随机事物！

ex.s: A recent survey on Chinese people's reading habits, based on a random sample of more than 10,000 people from 30 cities across China, revealed that the Chinese spend a lot of time reading.
ex.t: 最近一项关于中国人阅读习惯的调查，基于来自中国30个城市的一万多人随机抽样，显示中国人花了很多时间阅读。

ex.s: Each subject got eight reviews to read: a balanced set of two positive fake, two positive real, two negative fake and two negative real, presented in a random order.
ex.t: 每位受试者读了八条评论：均衡地包含两条正面虚假、两条正面真实、两条负面虚假和两条负面真实，以随机顺序呈现。
